bridges.burden: Show that a qualified Christian account remains plausible despite hiddenness and hell.
Explain salvation without a theology test.
Defend commitment under less than certainty.
Connect Christianity to virtue and freedom.
Offer morally plausible alternatives to eternal torment.
Identify goods that uncertainty could enable.
Argue that hiddenness and hell make a loving God implausible.
Show why sincere nonbelief conflicts with desired relationship.
Show why belief or practice cannot simply be chosen.
Challenge salvation conditions for unconvinced people.

sections.title: Probability, worldview comparison, and qualified Christianity
sections.weightRationale: This opening frame fixes the comparative evidential method and the first hiddenness challenge, but it is less developed than the later direct exchanges.

sections.title: Salvation, sincere seeking, and explicit belief
sections.weightRationale: The exchange directly tests whether qualified Christian inclusivism can answer the moral cost imposed on sincere nonbelievers.

sections.title: Practice, belief, and commitment under uncertainty
sections.weightRationale: This sustained practical dispute tests whether action can bridge involuntary nonbelief without already assuming a religious option is credible.

sections.title: Virtue, belief costs, and self-sacrifice
sections.weightRationale: Both speakers compare Christian formation with secular ethical pursuit and contest whether an eternal reward preserves genuine sacrifice.

sections.title: Chosen hell and Christlike substitution
sections.weightRationale: The speakers directly test a chosen-hell account with a demanding substitution hypothetical and its Christological parallel.

sections.title: Parental love, eternal torment, and annihilation
sections.weightRationale: This central exchange elicits a significant concession on eternal torment while showing that annihilation does not by itself resolve relational hiddenness.

sections.title: Freedom, certainty, prevalence, and the goods of hiddenness
sections.weightRationale: The longest final exchange develops the core motion through prevalence, freedom, relationship, cooperation, and the distinction between certainty and settled belief.
